column1: # boru Language Specification: edge-quote-1 — eval-by-default duality
# Edge cases for the quotation system's FIRST principle: lists are
# EVALUATED by default ([add 1 2] -> [3]); `quote` opts out and holds
# the tokens as data ((quote [add 1 2]) in canon); implicit-quote
# positions (if branches, for/each/fn bodies) hold code WITHOUT the
# quote wrapper; `def name [body]` is NOT such a position — it
# evaluates the node and binds the value. Expected values use the
# canon renderer. See EXPLANATION.md "Quotation and evaluation",

column3: evaluated by default: one element, the sum
the evaluated list has ONE element
held: canon renders the quote wrapper + the raw word
the held list has THREE nodes (word + two operands)
a literal element reads out as plain data
a held list is still a real List
plain data: nothing to run, eval is a no-op
plain data size unchanged by auto-eval
quoting plain data only adds the held marker
held plain data: same three elements
infix-form arithmetic evaluates inside a list literal
…but held it is three raw nodes
index 1 of the HELD list is the first operand (index 0 is the word)
the Word element re-fires at the pointer when pulled out bare
a numeric head reads out fine — only Word nodes re-fire
the evaluated list orders equal to [3]
inner lists evaluate too (recursively)
nesting inside an open stack: only list interiors evaluate
sibling inner lists evaluate independently
quote holds the WHOLE tree — inner list stays raw
held outer size counts the inner list as one node
two held inner lists, still two nodes
nested plain data unchanged
a word applying to a nested literal runs inside the list
a scalar passes through quote unchanged
a string passes through quote unchanged
`true` is captured as the ATOM true/q, not a Boolean
none passes through as the None value
a map is NOT held — quote passes it through as data
quote does NOT suppress a map value's ParenExpr eval
a paren EVALUATES first; quote marks the result
stack-form quote marks an already-evaluated data list
stack-form quote on a scalar is the identity
the first quote captures the TOKEN `quote`, stranding foo

column1: # --- §4 implicit-quote positions hold code; def EVALUATES ---------------

column3: an if branch is CODE: it runs and leaves 3, not [3]
the untaken branch never runs
a doomed branch is held code — untaken, it cannot raise
a for body is held code, re-run per iteration
…and each run evaluates the body afresh
an each body is held code applied per element
stack words in an each body see the pushed element
a fn body is held at def time — defining cannot raise
def is NOT an implicit-quote position: the list evaluates
…and the binding holds the one-element result
…the bound value's one element is the sum
quote restores the held form under def
a stored held list re-references as the held list
a held list nests as ONE element when re-collected
…and counts as one
a stored held list indexes like any list
…and types as a plain List
quote of a BOUND name still captures the NAME, not the value
referencing a stored held list does NOT run it (contrast `def h word [dup add]`)
hold, then run: do evaluates the held list
do's own body slot is implicit-quoted code
held infix-form arithmetic runs under do
do's result feeds the surrounding program
nested do: the inner result is the outer body's operand
an empty body contributes nothing
held code that itself quotes-and-does, one level down
defs inside held code bind when the code RUNS
do over a stored quote (the held code is a value)
a one-literal held program replays its literal
held code referencing a binding resolves when RUN

column1: def body (quote [add 1 2]) do body do body add
column3: a stored quote re-runs — held code is reusable
a list literal holding one quote evaluates to one element
do over a quote fetched back out of a container

column1: def ops [quote [2 mul 3] quote [10 sub 4]] do (ops get 1)
column3: the second stored program runs independently
quote-and-do INSIDE a list literal evaluates in place

column1: # --- §6 do reifies errors; open code unwinds ----------------------------

column3: a raise inside do REIFIES as an Error value on the stack
the reified value is a first-class Error

column1: def e (do [raise bad_code "m"]) e dot code
column3: the .code field of a reified error reads as its atom
binding the reified error keeps the Error type
nested do: the inner reified error passes through the outer body
two reified errors coexist as plain values

column1: def e (do [raise oh "m"]) e dot code case [oh/q "caught" "other"]
column3: dispatching on a reified error's code atom
a held raise is just three inert nodes — holding cannot raise
def EVALUATES its list — an unknown inner word errors at def time
a held fn body's unknown word raises when the fn RUNS
